sources.title: m3_check.py: matrices and exhaustive connectivity check for module m3
sources.venue: Script in this repository, written by module owner m3
sources.notes: Run with python3 -I; output saved in modules/m3_check.out. Integer matrix multiplication, brute-force walk enumeration for k = 1 to 4, BFS, exhaustive over all labelled simple graphs with N = 1 to 6. Checks the statement for small N; it is not a proof.

claims.text: For different vertices u and v, there is a (u,v)-walk iff there is a simple (u,v)-path (no repeated vertex). Proved by taking a shortest walk and cutting out any loop; also the textbook's Lemma 1.2.1 and Grinberg's Corollary 2.9.7.

support.quote: Ենթադրենք, որ G գրաֆում u-ն և v-ն իրարից տարբեր երկու գագաթներ են: Այդ դեպքում ցանկացած (u, v)-շրջանցումից կարելի է առանձնացնել պարզ (u, v)-ճանապարհ:
Assume that there is a walk from u to v of length k for some k ∈ N. Then, there is a path from u to v of length ≤ k.

claims.text: For different vertices u and v in a simple graph, a (u,v)-trail (the book's path, Def. 1.2.12) exists iff a simple (u,v)-path (Def. 1.2.13) exists iff a (u,v)-walk exists; so the book's Definition 2.1.1 and the course's path convention define the same connected graphs.

claims.text: A simple graph on N vertices is connected iff every off-diagonal entry of A + A^2 + ... + A^(N-1) is positive. Complete proof from walk counting (C5), the walk-to-path lemma (m3-C1) and the path-length bound N - 1 (C21). Paramadevan and Sotheeswaran state the result; their proof is not used.

support.quote: Then, AG is connected if and only if bij ≠ 0, when i ≠ j.
Let k be a positive integer. Then the entry in the (i, j)-position of the matrix A^k is the number of walks of length k from v_i to v_j in G.

claims.text: Every entry of (I + A)^(N-1) is positive iff every off-diagonal entry of A + ... + A^(N-1) is positive: by the binomial theorem (I and A commute) the matrix is the sum of C(N-1,k) A^k for k = 0..N-1, all coefficients at least 1; diagonal entries are always at least 1. Its entries are walk counts with binomial weights, not path counts.

support.quote: Let G be a simple graph on [n], and let A be the adjacency matrix of G. Then G is connected if and only if all the entries of (I_n + A)^(n−1) are positive.
Then G is connected if and only if the matrix power (I + A)^(n−1) has all entries strictly positive.

claims.derivation: modules/m3.md, Section 3.5, Theorem 3.4; check in modules/m3_check.out (binomial identity, equal: True)

claims.text: For i different from j, (A + ... + A^(N-1))_ij > 0 iff n_i and n_j lie in the same connectivity component; the off-diagonal zeros of the sum mark exactly the pairs in different components.

claims.text: A single power is not a test and the limit N - 1 cannot be lowered on a path graph. On the board graph (A^2)_12 = 0 although n1n2 is an edge, and (A^1)_13 = 0 while (A^2)_13 = 1. Reason: every edge joins {n1, n3} to {n2}, so walks from n1 to n2 have odd length. The claim that the end vertices of a path graph on N vertices are joined only by a path of length N - 1 is checked by script for N = 3 only.

support.quote: Let k be a positive integer. Then the entry in the (i, j)-position of the matrix A^k is the number of walks of length k from v_i to v_j in G.

claims.text: On the board graph (edges n1n2, n2n3) A = [[0,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]], A^2 = [[1,0,1],[0,2,0],[1,0,1]], A + A^2 = [[1,1,1],[1,2,1],[1,1,1]], (I+A)^2 = [[2,2,1],[2,3,2],[1,2,2]]: connected. For edge n1n2 only (n3 isolated) A + A^2 = [[1,1,0],[1,1,0],[0,0,0]] and (I+A)^2 = [[2,2,0],[2,2,0],[0,0,1]]: not connected. For the triangle A + A^2 has every entry 2 and (I+A)^2 every entry 3. Every matrix is computed by modules/m3_check.py and cross-checked against brute-force walk counts for k = 1 to 4.

support.quote: sum test says connected: True | power test: True | BFS: True

claims.derivation: modules/m3_check.py, output modules/m3_check.out; modules/m3.md Section 5.1 and 5.2

claims.text: For every labelled simple graph on N = 1 to 6 vertices (1, 2, 8, 64, 1024, 32768 graphs; 1, 1, 4, 38, 728, 26704 connected) the sum test, the (I+A)^(N-1) test and breadth-first search give the same answer. This checks the theorem for small N; it is not a proof.

The paper tests only pairs of different vertices; for u = v the book handles the case through the reflexivity of its path relation, and the book does not say whether a walk of length 0 exists. This reading of Definition 2.1.1 and of the board definition is the paper's own.

claims.text: Breadth-first search with adjacency lists costs O(n + m) (Waterloo CS 341 slide 8). Given only the matrix A, a search scans one row of N entries per dequeued vertex, so N^2 entries in all (derived, not sourced). The step 'G is connected iff all vertices are marked' is derived by the paper from the slide-11 statement and Lemma 3.1, not found in a source.
